classifiedFindings.title: Nudge token that becomes the payment token: the entire accumulated nudge pot is swept to an arbitrary batchMint caller via the ungated dust refund
classifiedFindings.footgunType: non-obvious owner configuration that unknowingly arms a permissionless theft path (Law 3 exception — classified by the impact it unlocks, NOT as centralization)

classification.assetImpact: The entire standing nudge pot — real USDC donated by prior minters and held on BatchNFTMinterMultiToken — leaves to an unprivileged caller. Measured: 190.0 of a 200 USDC pot in one call, plus a second 100 USDC on refill. Extraction is exactly pot - mintPrice, unbounded above by any protocol parameter; the loss scales with however much has accumulated.
attackPath: 1. PRECONDITION (owner, non-malicious, one routine tx): batch.setDispatcherIndex(i) selects a USDC-prime dispatcher, so _resolvePaymentPath derives USDC as the payment token while USDC is simultaneously on the nudge whitelist (isNudgeToken(USDC) == true). Three of the four in-scope dispatchers (NudgeRatchet, Uniboost, PromotionUniV2_Eth) are USDC-prime, so this is the majority choice, not an exotic one.
2. Honest minters fund the stream; a window elapses; the flush lands the pot on the batch-minter.
3. Any address calls batchMint(count = 1, recipient = self, paymentAmount = 1 wei, [0]). No role, no allowlist, no budget.
4. count(1) < nudgeSize(5) => qualifies == false => _payRewards never runs and the reward snapshot is all zero.

5. Value leaves through the step-10 dust sweep at BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:_snapshotRewards:558 / batchMint:479-486, which is NOT gated on qualifies: the whole payment-token balance is refunded to the caller.
6. The mint itself is funded out of the pot (step-6 grants nftMinter an unbounded allowance over the batch-minter's balance), so the attacker's 1 wei is nominal and the NFT is a bonus.
7. Repeat on every refill — permissionless first-come race, continuous while the configuration stands.
classification.likelihood: high once the precondition holds; the exploit step itself has zero preconditions, costs 1 wei, and is a PoC'd permissionless race. Likelihood of the precondition: MODERATE and honestly stated — the live configuration at d4cc563 does NOT resolve payment to USDC (the batch path prices in an 18-dp PAY token, per T4), so this is not exploitable at the current on-chain config. It requires one deliberate, ordinary owner tx. What makes it a real risk rather than a hypothetical is (a) setDispatcherIndex is a designed, routine mutator, (b) three of four in-scope dispatchers are USDC-prime so the hazardous selection is the statistically likely one, and (c) NOTHING warns: no guard rejects paymentToken ∈ nudgeWhitelist, no event, no view. The owner would have no reason to suspect the consequence.
classification.assumptions: The batch-minter's resolved payment token is also a nudge-whitelisted token. Non-zero pot standing on the batch-minter (the normal steady state — T3 measures resident/flushed balances continuously). nudgeSize > 1 (live value 5).
classification.externalRequirements: One owner transaction (setDispatcherIndex or setTokenMinter) selecting a USDC-prime dispatcher. No attacker privileges, no market conditions, no third-party cooperation, no capital.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: High: an unprivileged third party takes the whole pot for 1 wei, PoC'd on the real stack with a control arm proving 0 extraction before the repoint. The C4 High bar is 'assets can be stolen ... via a valid attack path that does not have hand-wavy hypotheticals' — the attack path contains no hypotheticals at all; only its enabling configuration is conditional, and that condition is a single routine owner action whose consequence is invisible. Per Law 3 a NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun is classified by the impact it unlocks (up to High for direct asset loss), and per the sanitizer this is explicitly NOT a centralization finding because the value is taken by a third party, not by the owner.
classifiedFindings.plausibilityJustification: Plausible, not Implausible: nothing extraordinary is required — no validator collusion, no economic black swan, no price manipulation. The enabling step is a normal admin operation the protocol exposes on purpose and whose hazardous variant is the majority of the available dispatchers.

doubt.reasoning: Medium is arguable on the ground that the value leak carries a stated assumption plus an external requirement (the owner repoint), which is literally the C4 Medium wording, and that the configuration is not live today. It was resolved to High because the loss is total and repeatable, the taker is unprivileged, the pot is other users' money, and the owner has no signal that the door is open — under Law 1 understating a PoC'd permissionless total-drain to keep the report tidy is the wrong error to make. If the owner can state that the payment path will never resolve to a nudge-whitelisted token AND lands a constructor/setter guard enforcing it, this collapses to Low (defence-in-depth). Flagged for human review.
doubt.collapseCondition: Add an on-chain guard rejecting paymentToken ∈ nudgeWhitelist (or gate the step-10 dust sweep on qualifies) — the guard is the fix and also the severity collapse.

classifiedFindings.scopeCaveat: Root-cause lines are in the project's own nested lib/phoenix-nft-staking (BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:_snapshotRewards:558, batchMint:479-486). Kept live under Law 1 as an integration hazard against the first-party dispatchers; mirrored upstream under XP-01 using the SAME fingerprint. Must remain live on at least one ledger at all times.
classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Upstream (phoenix-nft-staking): gate the step-10 dust sweep on `qualifies`, or exclude nudge-whitelisted balances from the dust refund. First-party (yield-claim-nft): reject a dispatcher selection whose prime token is nudge-whitelisted, and document the constraint in the dispatcher ops NatSpec.

classifiedFindings.title: NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.release() lands an unstreamed lump that a same-block back-runner captures in full; the story-046 anti-burst invariant is not enforced on the fifth donor
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessRoute: F-03-046 (spec-conformance report). Same root cause, Law-2 framing. NOT double-counted as a second security finding.

classification.assetImpact: The entire released lump is diverted from the population of honest batchers to a single searcher. Measured: 50,000 USDC captured 100% in the same block for a cost of 5 mint prices; the next honest batcher pays the same 5 mint costs and receives 0. Value does not leave the protocol's reward system — the captor is a qualifying batcher who pays mint prices — but it is diverted wholesale from the distribution the design intends, and the cost/reward ratio (5 mints for 50,000 USDC) makes the capture essentially free.
attackPath: 1. `releaser` submits release(), which transfers the accumulated lump DIRECTLY to the batch-minter (NudgeRatchetDelayRelease.sol:release:107-110) — bypassing the NudgeStreamer entirely.
2. release() is onlyReleaser but the transaction is public in the mempool; the landing of the lump is fully observable.
3. A searcher back-runs it in the SAME block (no vm.warp needed) with batchMint(count = 5, recipient = self, minRewards = [lump]).
4. minRewards set to the whole lump makes the capture risk-free: the searcher either takes everything or the tx reverts and they pay nothing but gas.
5. Pot emptied: usdc.balanceOf(searcher) == LUMP, usdc.balanceOf(batch) == 0.
classification.likelihood: high — no owner error, no misconfiguration, no unusual market state. release() is a routine, admin-timed operation on a public mempool and the payoff is large and deterministic. The contrast arm proves the exposure is specific to this path: the same 50,000 USDC routed through the streamer by NudgeRatchet yields the same-block back-runner exactly 0, with >= LUMP-1 still buffered.
classification.assumptions: A profit-seeking searcher observes the mempool (standard on Ethereum mainnet). The lump is materially larger than 5 mint prices (true by construction — that is the point of a delayed release).
classification.externalRequirements: None beyond an ordinary competitive mempool. No privileges, no capital beyond 5 mint prices.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Medium, at the top of the band: no assets are stolen in the C4 High sense — the captor performs the paid action the contract is designed to reward and receives it through the intended payout path, so there is no accounting break and no unauthorized withdrawal. What is impacted is the protocol's stated function: four contracts' NatSpec advertise the anti-burst property as system-wide, and this path defeats it, leaking the full value of every release to whoever wins one block race instead of to the batcher population. Value leak with stated assumptions and an external requirement (a searcher), which is the C4 Medium definition.

doubt.reasoning: High is arguable: 100% of a 50,000 USDC lump, PoC'd, no preconditions, honest users demonstrably receive 0. It was held at Medium because the recipient is a legitimate participant paying the required mint cost through the sanctioned reward path — this is capture/mis-distribution of an incentive, not theft of custodied assets — and because C4 has consistently treated same-block reward racing as Medium-class MEV. The severity would rise if the released lump were shown to be user-attributed rather than protocol-discretionary. Flagged for human review.
doubt.notCollapsible: DO NOT collapse into phoenix-nft-staking ledger 858e9e80 (same MEV class, different contract, different repo, different fingerprint). Suppressing here on a foreign wont-fix would be exactly the cross-ledger silent closure the fingerprint scheme exists to prevent (XP-02).

classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Route release() through the NudgeStreamer like the other four donors (registerStream + collectNudge) so the lump is rate-limited rather than instantaneous; or make release() private-orderflow-only, which mitigates but does not fix (the pot is still winner-take-all at the next batch).
crossRefs: L-12 (sibling entry, pause-does-not-freeze-custody — different class, do not collapse)
XP-03 (StableYieldAccumulator.claim() is the second unbuffered funding source)

classifiedFindings.ledgerLabel: L-08 (EXPIRED CLOSURE — reopen proposal; severity to be RAISED low -> medium on reopen)
classifiedFindings.title: NudgeRatchet's mandatory streamer wedges every mint and makes resident USDC unreachable; the L-08 fix is intact but its closure rationale expired
classifiedFindings.poc: workspace/yield-claim-nft/test/run19-Tier3Nudge.t.sol::Run19_T2_RatchetWedge (4/4 pass; test_T2c no-rescue negative carries a positive control; test_T2d blacklist arm)

classification.assetImpact: Two distinct impacts. (1) AVAILABILITY: while the streamer path is broken, EVERY user mint at that index reverts — NudgeRatchet is the only one of five donors with no try/catch, no donationSplit, and a batchMinter that cannot be zeroed, so there is no degraded mode. (2) STRANDED VALUE: any USDC resident on NudgeRatchet is unreachable by any actor — an owner raw call to rescueERC20(address,address,uint256) returns false (selector absent; positive control on a freshly deployed NudgeRatchetDelayRelease returns true), and the only forwarding path (_dispatch's full-balance sweep) is itself the thing that is reverting. Worse, T2d shows a USDC blacklist applied to the SHARED streamer bricks NudgeRatchet and Uniboost simultaneously AND permanently strands the already-buffered pooled funds (pullPendingStream reverts on _settle's outbound transfer; NudgeStreamer has no owner rescue at all — XP-05).
attackPath: TRIGGER A (config): nudgeStreamer == address(0) — the post-deploy default — => Error('NudgeRatchet: nudgeStreamer unset') on every dispatch.
TRIGGER B (config): the (batchMinter, USDC) pair is unregistered on the streamer => NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered(), selector-matched.

TRIGGER C (third party, no privileges): USDC blacklists the shared NudgeStreamer address. Inbound transferFrom reverts for every donor; outbound _settle reverts, so the pooled buffer becomes permanently unrecoverable.
In all cases the revert propagates ATokenDispatcherV2.dispatch -> NFTMinterV2._executeMint and the whole user mint reverts (balanceOf(user, idx) == 0 asserted).
Concurrently, any USDC already resident on the ratchet has no exit: no rescueERC20, and the sweep leg is the reverting leg.
classification.likelihood: medium. Triggers A and B are configuration states the protocol legitimately passes through (A is the literal post-deploy default) and are owner-recoverable once recognised — they fail loudly. Trigger C is external and low-probability but entirely outside anyone's control and, uniquely, IRREVERSIBLE: it strands the pooled buffer with no rescue anywhere in the call graph. The trigger set at d4cc563 is a strict superset of the pre-story-046 surface and now includes a third-party failure that did not previously exist.
classification.assumptions: USDC is the streamed token (true for three of four in-scope donors). NudgeStreamer is shared across donors (true).
classification.externalRequirements: For A/B: an owner configuration state. For C: a token-issuer blacklist action — external, uncontrollable, and the reason this is not purely an owner footgun.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Medium: assets are not stolen, but protocol availability is impaired outright (all mints at the index revert with no degraded mode) and value is stranded with no escape hatch for any actor. That is squarely the C4 Medium wording — function/availability impacted, value leak with stated assumptions and external requirements. It does not reach High because the dominant triggers are recoverable configuration states rather than an attacker-controlled path, and no third party gains what the protocol loses.
classifiedFindings.ledgerNote: EXPIRED CLOSURE, its OWN bucket — NOT a regression and NOT an incomplete fix. L-08's story-038 patch (the full-balance sweep at src/dispatchers/NudgeRatchet.sol:142-162) is INTACT at d4cc563. What expired is the closure's rationale: L-08 was closed explicitly 'on whether out-of-band USDC becomes recoverable, NOT on literal rescueERC20 presence', and story-046 turned the sweep's only delivery leg into an external cross-repo call that can revert. Severity on reopen is MEDIUM, not L-08's original Low: the strand is now unconditional in the failure state and is accompanied by a total availability wedge that did not exist when L-08 was filed.
classifiedFindings.criticalWarning: DO NOT tell any reviewer to restore the sweep — it is already there. The remedy is a NEW escape hatch (a real rescueERC20, or an owner sweep that does not depend on collectNudge succeeding) and/or a donation-disable so a mis-wire degrades instead of bricking.

doubt.note: Confident Medium. The only judgement call was inheritance: L-08 was Low, and an expired closure normally inherits at least its prior severity. Here the behaviour classified on its merits at d4cc563 is materially worse than what L-08 described (availability wedge + third-party-triggerable irreversible strand of the POOLED buffer), so it is raised, not inherited.

classifiedFindings.contingency: If the human DECLINES the L-08 reopen, the wedge half must still be filed as a new entry (fingerprint 03864c76…, basis NudgeRatchet.sol:_dispatch:mandatory-streamer-liveness-wedge) at MEDIUM. Declining the reopen must not erase both halves.
classifiedFindings.authorPreDeclaration: The contract NatSpec pre-declares the wedge 'NOT an audit finding'. Per Law 1 an author's say-so does not auto-suppress. The declaration covers the deliberate liveness coupling; it does NOT cover the second-order consequence (escape hatch omitted on a rationale that no longer holds), which is the load-bearing half.
classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Add rescueERC20 to NudgeRatchet (its own sibling NudgeRatchetDelayRelease already has it — the asymmetry is the bug); and/or add a donationEnabled/try-catch so a broken streamer degrades the donation instead of reverting the user's mint. Separately, XP-05: NudgeStreamer itself needs an owner rescue.

classifiedFindings.title: Retiring a (batchMinter, token) stream permanently strands one duration's donations; four routine tidy-up actions each close the only recovery path
classifiedFindings.footgunType: operational hazard — the harm is invisible at the moment of a well-intentioned, tidy owner action, and the project's OWN migration script performs the blind sequence
classifiedFindings.poc: sized empirically by Run19_T3_BufferResidency (6/6 pass): resident buffer converges to 99.98% of one stream window's inflow at 8 windows; delivered + resident == donated on every row; drains to exactly 0 one window after donations stop

classification.assetImpact: One stream duration's worth of donated USDC — B* = ρ·D, cadence-independent — becomes permanently unreachable. Measured range at the observed ~77.6 USDC per 40-batch: 11 to 4,656 USDC across the D × cadence grid. Permanence is the point: NudgeStreamer has NO owner rescue or sweep (verified exhaustively against its complete function list), so buffered value leaves only via _settle.
classification.attackPathNote: no attacker — this is an owner-sequencing hazard
attackPath: 1. Owner retires a stream by repointing setBatchMinter / setRecipient / setNudgeStreamer on any of the four dispatchers (routine migration hygiene).
2. Path 1 out of the buffer (a donor calling collectNudge for that pair) stops immediately — the donor no longer targets the old pair.

3. Path 2 (the old batchMinter calling pullPendingStream, which BatchNFTMinterMultiToken does in exactly ONE place, inside batchMint) still exists but requires ALL of: not paused · tokenMinter != 0 · dispatcherIndex != 0 · token still whitelisted · someone paying for >= 1 real mint.

4. Any ONE of four ordinary decommissioning actions destroys path 2 forever: pause(), setTokenMinter(0), setDispatcherIndex(0), or unwhitelisting the token. _resolvePaymentPath runs at step 2, BEFORE the step-3.5 flush, so unsetting either pointer reverts batchMint before the flush is even reached.
5. After that the buffer is unreachable by every actor including the owner.
classification.likelihood: medium-to-high at the next migration, and this is the decisive point: the project's EXISTING MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol retirement step recovers the pot via balanceOf(oldBatchMinter) — structurally blind to the streamer buffer, and it predates the streamer. An operator following the repo's own script trips this. Nothing surfaces the buffer: no event at retirement, no dispatcher view, and the only read is NudgeStreamer.pendingStream(oldBatchMinter, token), which a migration operator has no reason to call.
classification.assumptions: A stream retirement / batch-minter migration occurs (a planned, expected event on this protocol — three have already been scripted). The live stream `duration` is non-trivial; it is UNKNOWN in every reviewed repo (MR-01) and sizes the loss linearly.
classification.externalRequirements: None external — the sequence is entirely internal to normal operations.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Medium, as a Law-3 operational hazard classified by the impact it unlocks: value is permanently lost (not stolen), the loss is bounded but non-dust, and the triggering sequence is the one the repo's own migration script already performs. It is not High because there is no attacker, no theft, and correct-ordered recovery is cheap and available (wait >= D, one batchMint(1) flushes the whole buffer, then rescueERC20, ~13 USDS plus gas). It is not QA/Low because the harm is irreversible once the decommissioning tx lands and no signal exists at the decision point — a competent, non-malicious owner would be surprised, which is precisely the Law-3 test for keeping it in scope.

doubt.reasoning: Low is arguable if the live `duration` turns out to be short: at the bottom of the measured grid the exposure is ~11 USDC, which is dust and would make this a Low/QA ops note. Medium was chosen because the top of the grid is ~4,656 USDC, the loss is irreversible, and the parameter that decides it (MR-01) is unknown to the audit. Severity is therefore explicitly PARAMETER-DEPENDENT: supply the live `duration` and batch cadence and this can be re-pinned without re-analysis. Flagged for human review.

classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: Repoint the donor first -> wait >= duration -> read pendingStream and confirm -> one batchMint(1, …) on the old instance -> rescueERC20 -> ONLY THEN pause / unset tokenMinter / unset dispatcherIndex / unwhitelist. This belongs in the dispatchers' ops NatSpec and in MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol, which is currently blind to the buffer.
classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Emit an event carrying pendingStream at retirement, expose a dispatcher-side view of the buffer, add the buffer read to MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol, and (upstream, XP-05) give NudgeStreamer an owner rescue so the sequence stops being one-way.
crossRefs: MR-01 (unknown live duration — sizes this finding)
SIBLING: do NOT merge with CLASS-19-06 (same contract:function, different rootCauseClass)

classifiedFindings.title: A repoint (or enabling a dormant donation) silently arms NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered on every subsequent mint
classifiedFindings.footgunType: operational hazard — silent arming of a delayed, cross-repo-recoverable revert
classifiedFindings.poc: shares Run19_T2_RatchetWedge's NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered selector match; independently reproduced a fourth time by the Q-17 harness runtime failure on PromotionUniV2_Eth

classification.assetImpact: None directly. Availability only: user mints at the affected index revert until the registration is completed. No value is stranded (the revert is tx-atomic — the user's payment rolls back), and NFTMinterV2's config.disabled provides an owner backstop that keeps the rest of the system minting.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls setBatchMinter(new) / setRecipient(new) on a LIVE dispatcher, or enables a dormant donation. The call SUCCEEDS SILENTLY — no guard, no probe, no local view surfaces the missing stream registration.
2. Every subsequent user mint through that dispatcher reverts NudgeStreamer__NotRegistered().

3. Clearing it requires setNudgeTokenWhitelist on the batchMinter AND THEN registerStream on NudgeStreamer — a contract in a DIFFERENT repository that may not share the owner key, which is what extends the outage beyond one transaction.
classification.likelihood: medium — repoints are routine, and nothing warns. But the failure is immediate, loud and total on the very first user mint, so detection is near-instant.
classification.assumptions: The dispatcher is live and taking user traffic at the moment of the repoint.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner action; possibly a second key-holder to complete registerStream cross-repo.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Low: availability-only, tx-atomic, no value at risk, no unrecoverable state, loud and immediately visible, with a config.disabled backstop. It stays IN the report (rather than being suppressed under KI-1/KI-4) because the repoint sub-case is genuinely surprising — the arming is silent and the cure lives in another repository. The deploy-ordering sub-case was correctly suppressed (SUB-02): it fails on the first dispatch before any user traffic, so a competent owner is not surprised.

doubt.reasoning: Medium is arguable on the literal C4 wording 'availability could be impacted' — user minting at the index is fully down until fixed, and the cross-repo key dependency could make the outage last longer than one transaction. Low was chosen because the outage is self-inflicted by the owner, instantly and loudly detected, causes no user loss (payments revert atomically), and is recoverable by the owner alone with a documented backstop. If the second key-holder is genuinely a different party with a slow process, re-weigh to Medium. Flagged for human review.
doubt.notCollapsible: Kept deliberately SEPARATE from CLASS-19-02 (DEDUP-19-02): same pattern, different consequence, different fix. There it additionally strands funds with no rescue; here it is availability-only. And separate from CLASS-19-05 despite the same contract:function — different rootCauseClass, different fingerprint. DO NOT MERGE either pairing.

classifiedFindings.authorPreDeclaration: The shipped 'NOT an audit finding' NatSpec is CORRECT for deploy-ordering and OVER-BROAD for repoint. A story cannot pre-declare a hazard out of scope. Correct disposition: known, accepted, recorded as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance.
classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Have setBatchMinter/setRecipient probe the streamer (a view call asserting the (batchMinter, token) pair is registered) and revert or emit a warning event if not; or expose a dispatcher-side isStreamReady() view for the runbook.

classifiedFindings.title: BalancerPoolerV2: disabling the donation removes parked USDS from the retry loop; psm.gem() is read live from an owner-settable PSM
classifiedFindings.footgunType: operational hazard — two non-obvious consequences of ordinary configuration changes, both silent, both recoverable

classification.assetImpact: Value is relocated/idled, never lost or stolen, and phUSD backing is NOT impaired in either sub-instance (CV-07 / R-06). (a) USDS parked by an earlier caught failure stops being re-swept, stops being wrapped to sUSDS, stops being productive collateral and does not contribute to pool() — it sits idle on the contract. (b) A setPSM repoint to a different-gem PSM yields an unregistered pair => NotRegistered => caught => USDS parks behind a single DonationSkipped event.
attackPath: (a) 1. A donation attempt fails and is caught; USDS parks on the pooler. 2. Owner sets donationEnabled = false (an ordinary throttle-down decision). 3. The sweep-and-retry that recovers parked USDS lives INSIDE if (donationEnabled), so it never runs again. 4. The NatSpec (:257-261) presents re-sweeping as THE recovery mechanism without noting it is conditional. 5. Recovery requires the owner to know to call rescueERC20:437.

(b) 1. Owner repoints setPSM to a PSM with a different gem. 2. gem is read LIVE from ISkyPSM(psm).gem() on every call, so the (batchMinter, gem) stream pair silently becomes unregistered. 3. The revert is caught; USDS parks; one DonationSkipped is emitted — and per CLASS-19-08 that event is now the only signal there is.
classification.likelihood: low-to-medium. Both require an owner configuration change; neither is exotic (throttling the donation off, or repointing the PSM after a Sky upgrade). What makes them non-obvious is that the harm is silent — no revert, no user-visible failure, one generic event — and in (a) the documentation actively points the owner at the wrong recovery mechanism.
classification.assumptions: USDS is parked at the moment of the donation-disable (sub-instance a). The replacement PSM's gem differs from the registered stream token (sub-instance b).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner configuration action in both cases; a Sky PSM migration makes (b) realistic.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Low: no theft, no permanent loss, no availability impact on users (dispatch still succeeds — only the donation is skipped), and full recovery exists via rescueERC20:437. It is kept in scope rather than suppressed as an obvious misconfig because the failure mode is silent and single-event rather than loud — a competent owner would be surprised, satisfying the Law-3 keep test. BalancerPoolerV2 is the SOLE live-gem-read of the four dispatchers (PromotionUniV2_Eth pins USDC as a constant, NudgeRatchet pins a 6-dp immutable), so the asymmetry is a first-party defect, not a token-selection decision.

doubt.reasoning: Sub-instance (a) could be argued as a Medium value-leak if a large USDS balance were parked and the misdirecting NatSpec kept the owner from finding rescueERC20 for a long period. Held at Low because the funds remain fully under owner control at all times, the amount is bounded by the 15% batchDonationSize, and no third party benefits.

classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Move the sweep-and-retry outside the if (donationEnabled) gate (or add an unconditional owner sweep), correct the :257-261 NatSpec to state the conditionality, and pin gem at construction — or re-validate the stream registration inside setPSM — matching the other three dispatchers.
crossRefs: CLASS-19-08 (DonationSkipped is now the sole signal)

classifiedFindings.title: The dust branch went event-silent exactly as DonationSkipped became the sole signal for a much wider failure set
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessRoute: F-01-047 (spec-conformance report). Law-2 framing of the same root cause — the documented observability contract was not updated in the same commit. NOT double-counted as a second security finding.

classification.assetImpact: None. Observability only: _psmDonate is atomic, parked USDS is re-swept (except under CLASS-19-07(a)), and phUSD backing is NOT impaired (R-06 found no unbacked-phUSD path in any failure mode; CV-07 confirms the >=2:1 cushion holds under the new quiet-skip surface). What silently dies is the batch-minter reward while hook.onDispatch keeps accruing gross mint-debt.
attackPath: 1. `require(gemAmt > 0, 'BalancerPoolerV2: donation dust')` was replaced by `if (gemAmt > 0) { … }` (story-047 bullet 4 — an AUTHORISED change, and the guard itself is load-bearing and correct: it keeps NudgeStreamer__ZeroAmount() out of the catch).
2. The old require reverted into the caller's catch, which emitted DonationSkipped. The new if returns normally and emits NOTHING.

3. Simultaneously the caught region's CONTENTS widened to PSM + streamer wiring + the streamer's own outbound settle transfer, so every distinct wiring failure now collapses into one undifferentiated DonationSkipped.

4. The documentation was not updated and doubles down, telling operators to 'watch DonationSkipped and the contract's USDS balance' — advice that is now wrong for the dust branch and ambiguous for everything else.
5. The same event-silent shape exists NATIVELY at Uniboost.sol:246 and PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol:392.
classification.likelihood: certain — this is the current behaviour on every dust-sized donation, not a conditional path.
classification.assumptions: Operators rely on the documented monitoring contract (which the NatSpec instructs them to do).

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Low: state/observability handling and a documentation contract that no longer matches the code — squarely the C4 QA/Low band. It is placed at Low rather than pure QA because the degraded signal is load-bearing for CLASS-19-07, where a silent value-parking condition is now detectable only through the one event that has been made ambiguous. Authorisation of the change by story-047 is not disposal of its consequence.
classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Emit a distinct DonationDust (or DonationSkipped with a reason code) on the zero-amount branch; differentiate the catch by revert selector; and update the monitoring NatSpec in the same commit. Apply the same treatment natively at Uniboost:246 and PromotionUniV2_Eth:392.

classifiedFindings.title: Uniboost's prime token is unconstrained and now transits a foreign transferFrom + transfer pair with no failure isolation

classification.assetImpact: No exploit at the live USDC topology and no demonstrated loss. The impact is a weakening of guarantees: post-story-046 the donation branch has NO try/catch, so a live donation depends on TWO token movements inside a foreign contract instead of one leaf transfer, converting three previously contract-level premises into deployment policy simultaneously — the CV-06 read-only-reentrancy hook-free-token clearance, blacklist isolation, and the streamer's shared-balance solvency invariant.
attackPath: 1. NudgeRatchet and NudgeRatchetDelayRelease enforce decimals() == 6 at construction; Uniboost takes primeToken_ free with NO guard at all — an asymmetry against its own siblings.
2. Any future deployment with a non-6-dp or hook-bearing prime token silently removes the reentrancy clearance and the blacklist isolation that the other dispatchers get structurally.
3. With no try/catch, a failure in either of the two foreign token movements reverts the whole user dispatch rather than degrading.
classification.likelihood: low at the current deployment (USDC), rising with any future Uniboost instance on a different prime token — which is exactly the scenario the constructor is supposed to fence.
classification.assumptions: Future deployments may choose a different prime token; nothing in code prevents it.
classification.externalRequirements: A new Uniboost deployment with a different prime token.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Low: a deploy-time guard asymmetry and a loss of failure isolation, with no demonstrated exploit path at the live topology. KI-2 correctly removes the malicious-token vector and KI-3 / the C4 FoT rule remove the generic fee-on-transfer claim (SUB-03/SUB-04); what survives is first-party and independent of both — a sibling contract enforces a constraint this one does not.

doubt.note: MR-02 (cross-stream shared-balance solvency via an unrestricted prime) remains PARKED and unresolved — two tiers disagree on where the loss lands. This classification does NOT close MR-02; if MR-02 resolves in favour of the whole-streamer-solvency reading, that is a separate finding at a higher severity, not a re-weigh of this one.

classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Mirror NudgeRatchet's constructor guard on Uniboost, or scope-document the acceptable prime-token set and enforce it at deploy review. Restore failure isolation (try/catch) on the donation branch.

classifiedFindings.title: PromotionUniV2_Eth burns against the leg output but pools against the whole balance
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessRoute: documented-property deviation (NatSpec, not a story tag) — reported here at honest severity; noted for the spec-conformance report as a documentation-fidelity item.

classification.assetImpact: Bounded and non-extractive. phusdBurned = phusdAcquired / 2 uses Leg A's RETURN VALUE, while _addPhusdPromoLiquidity reads balanceOf(address(this)). Residual or donated phUSD is therefore pooled WITHOUT a matching burn, so the documented 'half burned, halves value-matched' property holds only for a contract that starts each pool() at zero. minLP bounds the outcome, so this is documentation fidelity and a drifting burn ratio, not a value leak.
attackPath: 1. phUSD is left resident on the dispatcher (partial prior execution) or donated to it by anyone.
2. pool() burns half of only the CURRENT leg's acquisition (pool:451-454).
3. _addPhusdPromoLiquidity (:463-467) pools the ENTIRE phUSD balance, including the residual/donated amount that was never burned against.
4. The realised burn-to-pool ratio drifts below the documented 1:1-of-halves property.
classification.likelihood: low — requires resident or donated phUSD; minLP caps the consequence in the unit that matters.
classification.assumptions: Non-zero starting phUSD balance at the time of pool().
classification.externalRequirements: A prior partial execution or a third-party donation.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: Low: a spec/documentation deviation with a bounded accounting-basis effect and no value leak (minLP bounds the outcome). C4 QA/Low explicitly covers 'function incorrect as to spec'.

doubt.reasoning: Pure QA is arguable since minLP bounds the outcome and no value escapes. Held at Low because the deviation is in a value-accounting property (burn ratio) that the protocol's economics documentation asserts, not merely in a comment.
doubt.notCollapsible: EXPLICITLY NOT folded into L-13 / DEDUP-19-04 despite the identical whole-balance shape: different asset (phUSD / promotion token, not ETH), different consequence (documentation fidelity, not slippage-floor dilution), different fix. Folding it in would silently retire it under an owner decision that was NEVER MADE ABOUT IT. Also distinct from L-15 (same contract:function, different rootCauseClass).

classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Burn against the same basis you pool against — either burn half of balanceOf(address(this)), or pool only the leg's own output — and state which basis the documented property refers to.

classifiedFindings.title: The streamer forceApprove is the sole unpaired approval in these contracts
classifiedFindings.exploitabilityRefuted: R-03 — collectNudge:149 pulls exactly `amount` in the same call; any failure rolls back atomically. A residual allowance would require an under-pulling collectNudge, reachable only by an owner repointing setNudgeStreamer at a hostile contract, which is an OBVIOUS knowing owner action and correctly suppressed under Law 3 (SUB-05).

classification.assetImpact: None today. Hardening only: every OTHER forceApprove in these four contracts is paired with a zeroing reset (Uniboost:275/279, 300/306; PromotionUniV2_Eth:466/472, 483/485, 503/507; BalancerPoolerV2:336), and the streamer approve (BalancerPoolerV2:346, plus NudgeRatchet:160, Uniboost:250, PromotionUniV2_Eth:396) is the sole unpaired one. The safe-today property rests on an EXTERNAL, CROSS-REPO contract's implementation detail rather than on any local invariant.
attackPath: No exploit path. Retained as a defence-in-depth asymmetry, not a vector.
classification.likelihood: n/a — no exploit path exists at d4cc563.
classification.assumptions: NudgeStreamer.collectNudge continues to pull exactly the approved amount in the same call.

classifiedFindings.severityJustification: QA: no vector, exploitability affirmatively refuted in-run, retained purely as a cheap consistency hardening. This is explicitly NOT the C4 known-invalid approve-race / safeApprove front-running pattern — that pattern concerns a race on the allowance itself; the claim here is a structural asymmetry whose safety depends on a foreign contract.
classifiedFindings.recommendedRemediation: Pair each streamer approve with a zeroing reset, as every other forceApprove in these contracts already does.

classification.assetImpact: A third party extracts ETH that would otherwise have stayed with the protocol. Measured: +0.296774 ETH to a sandwicher; 11.00x dilution of the pooler's slippage floor; address(disp).balance == 0 afterwards, proving the ENTIRE balance was swapped rather than the leg output.
attackPath: 1. ETH is resident on PromotionUniV2_Eth — either left by a partial Leg B (rescueETH's own NatSpec concedes this) or sent by anyone through the open receive():589.
2. An honest off-chain pooler computes minPromoOut for the LEG's own ETH (478.315e18 in the test, 1% tolerance) and calls pool().
3. _legB:509-512 swaps address(this).balance — the whole balance, not the leg output — so minPromoOut now bounds a trade 11x larger than the one it was priced for.

4. A sandwicher front-runs with 12 ETH. CONTROL (T5b, zero stray): pool() REVERTS UniswapV2Router: INSUFFICIENT_OUTPUT_AMOUNT — the floor does its job and the sandwich is rejected. TREATMENT (T5c, 1.61794 ETH stray, identical floor, identical sandwich): pool() SUCCEEDS and the sandwicher exits +0.296774 ETH.
classification.likelihood: medium, and the two arms differ sharply. ATTACKER-FUNDED ARM: an attacker who supplies the stray ETH themselves donates 1.61794 ETH permanently into protocol-owned LP to earn 0.296774 ETH of sandwich profit — NET NEGATIVE for the attacker by ~1.32 ETH, so it is not self-financing and should not be presented to the owner as a profitable standalone attack. STALE-RESIDUAL ARM: where the stray ETH is already resident from a partial Leg B, the sandwich needs no donation at all and is free profit at protocol expense — this is the arm that carries the severity.
classification.assumptions: Stray ETH is resident on the dispatcher at the moment pool() is called (from a partial Leg B, or a donation). The pooler prices minPromoOut off the leg's own expected output, which is what an honest pooler does.
classification.externalRequirements: A mempool sandwicher; a non-zero resident ETH balance.

shadowClassifications.shadowSeverityJustification: Medium if reopened: value leaks to a third party under a stated assumption (resident ETH) with an external requirement (a sandwicher), and the protocol's own slippage floor — the control it relies on — is dilutable by an input nobody intended. It does NOT reach High because the profitable arm requires a pre-existing residual the attacker cannot reliably create at a profit, and the donated ETH itself still reaches protocol-owned LP exactly as the owner's triage found.
shadowClassifications.basisForReTriage: The load-bearing clause of the owner's wont-fix is: 'Non-theft (Tier-3 INV-4 fork-proved donated ETH only ever reaches protocol-owned LP, NEVER A THIRD PARTY).' The T5b/T5c differential contradicts that clause directly — a third party captures +0.296774 ETH in a scenario identical but for the stray balance. The loss channel is NOT the donated ETH's destination (which is indeed protocol-owned LP, exactly as INV-4 found) — it is the 11x dilution of the slippage floor, which INV-4 never tested: the same sandwich the honest floor REJECTS becomes ACCEPTED purely because of ETH the pooler did not put there.
shadowClassifications.action: RECOMMEND ONLY. Surface to the owner for re-triage of L-13 and its twin F-01-044 with the T5b/T5c differential attached. Apply the run19Note and the lastSeenRun bump; do NOT change status, do NOT mint a new fingerprint, do NOT overwrite triageReason or footgunNote. If the owner reaffirms wont-fix, record the T5 evidence on the entry so the 'never a third party' clause is CORRECTED rather than left standing as fact.

doubt.reasoning: Low is defensible given that the attacker-funded arm is net-negative for the attacker and the profitable arm depends on a residual the protocol can simply sweep. Medium was chosen because the stale-residual arm needs no attacker action at all beyond the sandwich, and because a slippage floor that can be silently made 11x too loose is a control failure rather than a parameter choice. The owner's operational note ('sweep/rescue stray ETH before authorizing a pool() call') is, in effect, the mitigation — if it is made a hard precondition in the pooler runbook or enforced on-chain, Low is correct.
